newsitem.title: IRAQ: China next in line to secure Iraqi oilfield rights.
newsitem.headline: China next in line to secure Iraqi oilfield rights.

text.p: China is expected soon to follow Russia and reach agreement with Baghdad for the development of Iraqi oilfields, a senior Iraqi oil official said on Wednesday.

A delegation from the Chinese National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) is expected soon in Baghdad to lay down the framework for an agreement to develop the billion barrel Ahdab field, the official said.
No precise time for the visit was mentioned.
China also has moved into contention as the leading candidate for the prized Halfaya field in southern Iraq, the official said.
China had recently made a bid for the field, discovered some 20 years ago and believed to hold commercial reserves of about five billion barrels, the official added.
Iraq believes the field could produce some 250,000 barrels a day (bpd) at full capacity.
Talks with the Chinese on Halfaya would take place in Baghdad alongside the discussions for Ahdab oilfield but any final agreement was likely to take longer, he said.
If the talks go smoothly China could beat Italy's Agip SpA SpA and India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp to Halfaya. Both have been mentioned in connection with the field.
Three weeks ago, three Russian companies secured the rights to develop eight billion barrels of Iraqi reserves held in the giant southern Qurana field.
Russia's LUKoil has a majority 52.5 percent stake with two other Russian companies holding 22.5 percent between them and Iraq 25 percent.
Iraq has been encouraging potential oil production partners to sign upstream agreements despite a U.N. ban on investment which will postpone the lion's share of any work until sanctions are lifted.
Investment in Iraq is banned under the U.N. embargo imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
French Elf Aquitaine and Total have agreed in principle with Iraq to sign for development respectively of the Majnoon and Nahr Umar fields once sanctions are lifted.
